Every year, governments allocate public money to research whose practical payoff is uncertain, distant, or entirely unknown at the moment of funding. I want to take that objection seriously rather than wave it away. The case for curiosity-driven research is strong, but it is not unconditional, and the honest version of it admits real costs and real failures. What follows is an attempt at the honest version.

### What we mean by curiosity-driven research

By curiosity-driven, or basic, research I mean inquiry whose primary aim is understanding rather than application. The distinction is not perfectly sharp. Plenty of applied work generates deep understanding, and plenty of basic work is done with a half-formed eye on eventual use. The cleaner way to draw the line is by the criterion used to decide what to fund. Applied research is justified by a problem it is meant to solve. Basic research is justified by a question it is meant to answer, with no commitment that the answer will be useful.

This matters because the two kinds of work fail differently and pay off differently. Applied research that fails to solve its problem has failed on its own terms. Basic research that fails to find a use has not necessarily failed at all, because use was never the standard. The standard was whether we now understand something we did not before. A society that funds only the first kind has quietly decided that understanding has no value unless it can be cashed in, and that is a decision worth examining rather than assuming.

### The argument from serendipity

The most frequently cited case for basic research is that the most valuable applications often come from work that was not aiming at them. The examples are familiar. The mathematics of number theory, pursued for centuries as the purest of pure inquiry, now secures every online transaction through public-key cryptography. The study of bacterial immune systems, an esoteric corner of microbiology, produced CRISPR gene editing. Investigations into the strange behaviour of light and matter at small scales gave us the laser, which was for years a solution in search of a problem and is now in every checkout scanner and fibre-optic cable.

The serendipity argument is genuinely strong, but it is also frequently overstated, and the overstatement is worth flagging because it weakens the case when critics notice it. The fact that some basic research led to enormous applications does not show that basic research is a reliable route to applications. It may be that the famous cases are famous precisely because they are rare, and that for every number theory there are a thousand lines of inquiry that led nowhere of practical consequence. The serendipity argument, taken alone, suffers from survivorship bias. We remember the lottery winners and forget the tickets.

So the argument has to be made more carefully. The defensible version is not that basic research reliably produces applications, but that applications of the largest kind, the ones that reshape whole industries, disproportionately trace back to work that could not have been justified by its eventual use, because that use was unimaginable at the time. If that is true, and the historical record gives reasonable support to it, then a funding system that demands a foreseeable application as a condition of funding will systematically miss exactly the largest payoffs. It will fund the foreseeable and starve the transformative. The serendipity argument, properly stated, is not about averages. It is about the shape of the tail.

### The argument from time horizons

Closely related is the problem of time. The lag between a basic discovery and its application is often measured in decades. The geometry that Riemann developed in the 1850s sat unused by physics until Einstein needed it for general relativity sixty years later. The work on the quantum behaviour of semiconductors that underpins the modern computer drew on physics from the early twentieth century. These horizons are far longer than any electoral cycle, any venture-capital fund's lifetime, and most corporate planning windows.

This creates a straightforward market failure of the textbook kind. A private firm cannot capture the returns on an investment that will pay off in forty years, possibly to a competitor, possibly in an industry that does not yet exist. The returns are real but they are diffuse, delayed, and uncapturable by the investor. Under those conditions, private actors will rationally underinvest, not because they are short-sighted but because they are responding correctly to the incentives they face. This is the classic justification for public provision of a public good, and basic knowledge fits the definition unusually well. Once discovered, a piece of knowledge can be used by everyone at once without being used up, which is the textbook property of non-rivalry, and it is very hard to exclude others from using it, which is non-excludability. Goods with both properties are chronically undersupplied by markets, and the standard remedy is public funding.

The time-horizon argument is, to my mind, the strongest part of the case, because it does not depend on cherry-picked success stories. It is a structural claim about incentives that holds regardless of how often basic research succeeds. Even a sceptic who doubts the serendipity stories should accept that if long-horizon knowledge has value, the private sector will underprovide it, and someone with a longer horizon must step in. The natural candidate is the public, acting through the state, because the public is the entity whose horizon is, in principle, indefinite.

### The argument from public good and shared inheritance

There is a third argument that is less often made and is, I think, underrated. Knowledge is part of the inheritance a society passes to its successors. We did not invent the calculus, or the structure of DNA, or the periodic table; we received them, and we will pass on whatever we add. A generation that consumed the scientific inheritance of its predecessors while adding nothing, because it judged that addition insufficiently profitable, would be living off capital it did not replenish. There is something both unjust and imprudent in that posture, in the way that there is something wrong with a generation that lets the cathedrals it inherited fall down because it would rather not pay the maintenance.

This argument is more value-laden than the others, and a hard-headed reader may find it soft. I include it not because it can carry the case alone but because the case is not purely economic. When defenders of basic science pretend that every grant is secretly an investment with a positive expected monetary return, they concede the very ground they should be contesting, which is that money is the only measure that counts.

### A Message from our Chief Executive

At NorthStar Beverages, sustainability is not a department. It is a mindset, a promise, and a journey we take together with every one of our stakeholders. As I reflect on all that our passionate teams have accomplished, I am filled with pride and optimism for the road ahead.

### Our Sustainability Pillars

Our approach rests on four pillars that guide every decision we make. Together, they form the foundation of a more sustainable and equitable future for all.

**Planet.** We are dedicated to minimising our environmental footprint across our entire value chain. From farm to shelf, we are working tirelessly to use resources wisely and to leave the world better than we found it.

**People.** Our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and empowering workplace where everyone can thrive and bring their whole selves to work.

**Communities.** We are proud to be a positive presence in the hundreds of communities where we operate. Through partnership and investment, we are helping local people build brighter futures.

Through a range of initiatives across our operations, we have driven down our carbon intensity and improved the efficiency of our facilities. Several of our plants have adopted energy-saving measures, and we have begun the transition towards cleaner energy sources at a number of sites.

We have also invested in high-quality carbon offset programmes that support reforestation and conservation around the world. These investments allow us to take responsibility for our footprint while contributing to a healthier planet. We are confident that, together with our partners, we can build a future where growth and sustainability go hand in hand.

Looking ahead, we will continue to explore innovative solutions to reduce our impact. Climate action is a marathon, not a sprint, and we are in it for the long haul.

We are working hard to improve our water efficiency and to give back more than we take. Across our operations, we have implemented water-saving technologies and best practices that are making a real difference. In water-stressed regions in particular, we are mindful of our impact and committed to being a good neighbour.

We have partnered with leading organisations on community water projects that bring clean water to people who need it most. These projects are a source of enormous pride for everyone at NorthStar, and they reflect our deep belief that access to clean water is a fundamental human right. We look forward to expanding our positive impact in the years to come.

We know that packaging is one of the areas where consumers most want to see change, and we are listening. NorthStar is committed to a world without waste, where every package has a second life.

We have made our bottles more sustainable through thoughtful design, using less material where we can and incorporating recycled content into our packaging. We are proud that our flagship bottle is now lighter than ever, reducing the resources needed to produce and transport it. We are also exploring exciting new materials and formats that could transform the way our products are packaged.

We firmly believe in the power of recycling, and we are working with partners across the industry to improve recycling rates and infrastructure. Our vision is a true circular economy, where the materials we use are kept in use for as long as possible. It is an ambitious vision, but we have never been afraid of ambition.

The journey to sustainability begins at the source. We are committed to sourcing our ingredients responsibly, with respect for the farmers who grow them and the land that sustains them.

We work closely with our agricultural partners to promote practices that are good for people and good for the planet. From the sugar in our drinks to the fruit in our juices, we want every ingredient to tell a story we can be proud of. We are increasing the share of our key ingredients that are sourced in line with our responsible sourcing principles, and we are encouraged by the progress our suppliers are making.

We believe that strong, long-term relationships with our suppliers are the key to a resilient and sustainable supply chain. By investing in our partners, we are investing in the future of our business and the communities that depend on it.

We are also proud to champion regenerative agriculture, an approach that holds enormous promise for soil health, biodiversity, and farmer livelihoods. We have begun working with a number of forward-thinking growers to explore how regenerative practices can be woven into our supply chain, and the early signs are genuinely inspiring. We believe this is the future of farming, and we intend to be at the forefront of it.

Nature is the foundation of everything we make. Without healthy ecosystems there would be no clean water, no fertile soil, and no thriving communities to enjoy our products. That is why protecting and restoring nature is so close to our hearts.

We are committed to being a positive force for biodiversity wherever we operate. We support a range of initiatives that protect habitats, restore landscapes, and safeguard the rich web of life that sustains us all. From planting trees to protecting watersheds, we are doing our part to help nature flourish for generations to come.

We recognise that the challenges facing the natural world are immense, and no single company can solve them alone. That is why we are proud to collaborate with conservation partners, civil society, and local communities to amplify our impact. Together, we can turn the tide for nature, and we are determined to be part of the solution.

### Innovation for Good

Innovation has always been in our DNA. We believe that the same spirit of creativity that gives the world products it loves can also help solve some of the planet's most pressing challenges. That is why we are investing in the ideas, technologies, and partnerships that will shape a more sustainable future.

Across our business, our teams are reimagining what is possible, from cleaner production methods to smarter ways of working. We are exploring exciting frontiers in materials science, renewable energy, and digital tools that help us understand and reduce our impact. We are energised by the possibilities, and we are committed to turning bold ideas into real-world progress.

We also know that the best ideas often come from unexpected places. That is why we engage with start-ups, universities, and innovators around the world, seeking out fresh thinking and new perspectives. By opening our doors to collaboration, we are accelerating the pace of change and building a more sustainable business for tomorrow.

### Engaging our Consumers

Sustainability is a shared journey, and our consumers are essential partners on the road ahead. Every day, millions of people choose NorthStar, and with that trust comes a responsibility to help them make choices that are good for them and good for the planet.

We are committed to giving our consumers the information and inspiration they need to play their part. Through our packaging, our marketing, and our digital channels, we are raising awareness of the issues that matter and encouraging more sustainable behaviours. We believe that small actions, multiplied by millions, can add up to extraordinary change.

We are also listening more closely than ever to what our consumers tell us. Their feedback shapes our priorities and pushes us to do better. We are humbled by their passion for the planet, and we are determined to be worthy of their trust.

### A Healthier Portfolio

We believe that great taste and wellbeing can go hand in hand. As tastes evolve and people seek to live healthier lives, we are proud to be evolving alongside them, offering a portfolio that gives people more of what they want and helps them feel good about their choices.

We have continued to broaden our range of options, introducing new flavours and formats designed with wellbeing in mind. We are giving consumers more choice than ever, including options with less sugar, and we are committed to clear, helpful labelling that empowers people to choose what is right for them. We want every consumer to feel that NorthStar has something for them, whatever the occasion.

Reformulating much-loved products is never easy, and we approach it with care and respect for the recipes people cherish. But we are determined to keep innovating, because we believe that doing right by our consumers and doing right by the world are one and the same. The journey towards a healthier portfolio is ongoing, and we are excited about where it will take us.

### Partnerships and Collaboration

We have always believed that the biggest challenges call for the broadest coalitions. None of us can build a sustainable future alone, and we are proud to stand shoulder to shoulder with partners who share our ambition and our values.

This year we deepened our collaboration with industry groups, non-governmental organisations, and public bodies working on the issues that matter most. By pooling our knowledge, our resources, and our reach, we are able to achieve far more together than any of us could achieve apart. These partnerships are at the very heart of how we drive change, and we are grateful for the trust and shared purpose that make them possible.

We are also committed to playing our part in the wider conversation about sustainability. We engage constructively with policymakers and stakeholders, sharing our perspective and learning from others, because we believe that progress comes from dialogue, openness, and a willingness to work together towards common goals.

### Transparency and Reporting

We know that trust must be earned, and that words must be matched by action. We are committed to being open about our journey, sharing both our achievements and the areas where we have more to do. Sustainability is not about perfection; it is about honest effort and continuous improvement, and that is the spirit in which we report our progress.

We will continue to refine how we measure and communicate our impact, drawing on emerging best practice and the expectations of our stakeholders. We want our reporting to be clear, meaningful, and genuinely useful to the many people who care about our journey. As our approach matures, so too will the way we tell our story.

Above all, we want our stakeholders to know that we take our responsibilities seriously, and that we are committed to being held to account. We welcome scrutiny, and we see it as a vital part of getting better, year after year.

### Our People and Communities

People are at the centre of everything we do. We are building a culture where every colleague feels valued, respected, and inspired to do their best work. Diversity and inclusion are not just the right thing to do; they make us stronger, more creative, and more connected to the consumers we serve.

This year we continued our investment in training and development, helping our people grow their skills and advance their careers. We are committed to health, safety, and wellbeing across our operations, because nothing matters more than the people who make NorthStar what it is.

In our communities, we are proud to support a wide range of causes through volunteering, partnerships, and charitable giving. Our colleagues gave generously of their time and talent this year, rolling up their sleeves to make a difference where it matters most. From youth education to disaster relief, we show up for the communities that have given us so much.

### Governance and Ethics

Trust is the foundation of our business. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and accountability in everything we do. Our governance framework ensures that sustainability is embedded at every level of the organisation, from the boardroom to the factory floor.

We are committed to doing business the right way, always. Our code of conduct guides our people to make ethical decisions every day, and we have robust processes in place to uphold our values. We engage openly with our stakeholders and welcome their input as we continue on our sustainability journey.

### Awards and Recognition

We are honoured that our efforts have been recognised by a number of organisations this year. These accolades are a testament to the hard work and dedication of our teams, and they inspire us to reach even higher. While awards are never the goal, they are a welcome affirmation that we are on the right track.

### Looking Ahead

We are proud of how far we have come, but we know our journey is far from over. The road ahead will not always be easy, and we will face challenges along the way. But we are more committed than ever to our vision of a brighter, more sustainable tomorrow.

In the year to come, we will deepen our commitments, strengthen our partnerships, and accelerate our progress. We will continue to listen, to learn, and to lead. And we will do it all with the optimism, passion, and purpose that define who we are.

Sustainability is the journey of a lifetime, and we are just getting started. Together, we can build a brighter tomorrow, one refreshing moment at a time. Thank you for being part of our story.

### About this Report

This report covers our global operations for the financial year. It reflects our ongoing commitment to transparency and to keeping our stakeholders informed about our sustainability journey. We welcome your feedback and look forward to sharing our continued progress in future reports.

Our colleagues gave generously of their time and talent this year, rolling up their sleeves to make a difference where it matters most. These accolades are a testament to the hard work and dedication of our teams, and they inspire us to reach even higher. While awards are never the goal, they are a welcome affirmation that we are on the right track.

We are proud of how far we have come, but we know our journey is far from over. The road ahead will not always be easy, and we will face challenges along the way. But we are more committed than ever to our vision of a brighter, more sustainable tomorrow.

In the year to come, we will deepen our commitments, strengthen our partnerships, and accelerate our progress. We will continue to listen, to learn, and to lead. And we will do it all with the optimism, passion, and purpose that define who we are.

Our approach rests on four pillars that guide every decision we make. Together, they form the foundation of a more sustainable and equitable future for all.

**Planet.** We are dedicated to minimising our environmental footprint across our entire value chain. From farm to shelf, we are working tirelessly to use resources wisely and to leave the world better than we found it.

**People.** Our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and empowering workplace where everyone can thrive and bring their whole selves to work.

**Communities.** We are proud to be a positive presence in the hundreds of communities where we operate. Through partnership and investment, we are helping local people build brighter futures.

NorthStar is deeply committed to climate action. We recognise the urgency of the climate challenge and we are determined to play our part. That is why we have set an ambitious goal to become carbon neutral, and we are making meaningful strides towards a low-carbon future.

Through a range of initiatives across our operations, we have driven down our carbon intensity and improved the efficiency of our facilities. Several of our plants have adopted energy-saving measures, and we have begun the transition towards cleaner energy sources at a number of sites.

We have also invested in high-quality carbon offset programmes that support reforestation and conservation around the world. These investments allow us to take responsibility for our footprint while contributing to a healthier planet. We are confident that, together with our partners, we can build a future where growth and sustainability go hand in hand.

Looking ahead, we will continue to explore innovative solutions to reduce our impact. Climate action is a marathon, not a sprint, and we are in it for the long haul.

Water is at the heart of our business and at the heart of life itself. As a beverage company, we have a special responsibility to be exemplary stewards of this precious resource, and we embrace that responsibility wholeheartedly.

Across our operations, we have implemented water-saving technologies and best practices that are making a real difference. In water-stressed regions in particular, we are mindful of our impact and committed to being a good neighbour.

We have partnered with leading organisations on community water projects that bring clean water to people who need it most. These projects are a source of enormous pride for everyone at NorthStar, and they reflect our deep belief that access to clean water is a fundamental human right. We are proud that our flagship bottle is now lighter than ever, reducing the resources needed to produce and transport it. We are also exploring exciting new materials and formats that could transform the way our products are packaged.

We firmly believe in the power of recycling, and we are working with partners across the industry to improve recycling rates and infrastructure. The journey to sustainability begins at the source. We are committed to sourcing our ingredients responsibly, with respect for the farmers who grow them and the land that sustains them.

Through our packaging, our marketing, and our digital channels, we are raising awareness of the issues that matter and encouraging more sustainable behaviours. ### Transparency and Reporting

People are at the centre of everything we do. We are building a culture where every colleague feels valued, respected, and inspired to do their best work. Diversity and inclusion are not just the right thing to do; they make us stronger, more creative, and more connected to the consumers we serve.

This year we continued our investment in training and development, helping our people grow their skills and advance their careers. We are committed to health, safety, and wellbeing across our operations, because nothing matters more than the people who make NorthStar what it is.

In our communities, we are proud to support a wide range of causes through volunteering, partnerships, and charitable giving. Our colleagues gave generously of their time and talent this year, rolling up their sleeves to make a difference where it matters most. From youth education to disaster relief, we show up for the communities that have given us so much.

Trust is the foundation of our business. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and accountability in everything we do. Our governance framework ensures that sustainability is embedded at every level of the organisation, from the boardroom to the factory floor.

We are committed to doing business the right way, always. Our code of conduct guides our people to make ethical decisions every day, and we have robust processes in place to uphold our values. We engage openly with our stakeholders and welcome their input as we continue on our sustainability journey.

We are honoured that our efforts have been recognised by a number of organisations this year. These accolades are a testament to the hard work and dedication of our teams, and they inspire us to reach even higher. While awards are never the goal, they are a welcome affirmation that we are on the right track.

In the year to come, we will deepen our commitments, strengthen our partnerships, and accelerate our progress. We will continue to listen, to learn, and to lead. And we will do it all with the optimism, passion, and purpose that define who we are.

Sustainability is the journey of a lifetime, and we are just getting started. Together, we can build a brighter tomorrow, one refreshing moment at a time. Thank you for being part of our story.

# Building a Brighter Tomorrow

## NorthStar Beverages plc - Annual Sustainability Report

### A Message from our Chief Executive

At NorthStar Beverages, sustainability is not a department. It is a mindset, a promise, and a journey we take together with every one of our stakeholders. This past year has been one of remarkable progress on our path to becoming the most responsible beverage company in the world. As I reflect on all that our passionate teams have accomplished, I am filled with pride and optimism for the road ahead.

We believe that doing well and doing good are two sides of the same coin. That conviction runs through everything we do, from the water we source to the communities we serve. Our purpose is simple but powerful: to refresh the world while protecting the planet that makes refreshment possible. In the pages that follow, you will see how we are turning that purpose into action, one bottle at a time.

The challenges facing our planet are real, and we do not take them lightly. But we are optimists by nature, and we firmly believe that business can be a force for good. NorthStar is committed to leading the way. Thank you for joining us on this incredible journey.

### Our Sustainability Pillars

Our approach rests on four pillars that guide every decision we make. Together, they form the foundation of a more sustainable and equitable future for all.

**Planet.** We are dedicated to minimising our environmental footprint across our entire value chain. From farm to shelf, we are working tirelessly to use resources wisely and to leave the world better than we found it.

**People.** Our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and empowering workplace where everyone can thrive and bring their whole selves to work.

**Communities.** We are proud to be a positive presence in the hundreds of communities where we operate. Through partnership and investment, we are helping local people build brighter futures.

**Product.** We are reimagining our products to be better for consumers and better for the planet, delivering the great taste people love with a lighter touch on the earth.

### Climate and Carbon

NorthStar is deeply committed to climate action. We recognise the urgency of the climate challenge and we are determined to play our part. That is why we have set an ambitious goal to become carbon neutral, and we are making meaningful strides towards a low-carbon future.

This year, we are proud to report significant progress on emissions. Through a range of initiatives across our operations, we have driven down our carbon intensity and improved the efficiency of our facilities. Several of our plants have adopted energy-saving measures, and we have begun the transition towards cleaner energy sources at a number of sites.

We have also invested in high-quality carbon offset programmes that support reforestation and conservation around the world. These investments allow us to take responsibility for our footprint while contributing to a healthier planet. We are confident that, together with our partners, we can build a future where growth and sustainability go hand in hand.

Looking ahead, we will continue to explore innovative solutions to reduce our impact. Climate action is a marathon, not a sprint, and we are in it for the long haul.

### Water Stewardship

Water is at the heart of our business and at the heart of life itself. As a beverage company, we have a special responsibility to be exemplary stewards of this precious resource, and we embrace that responsibility wholeheartedly.

We are working hard to improve our water efficiency and to give back more than we take. Across our operations, we have implemented water-saving technologies and best practices that are making a real difference. In water-stressed regions in particular, we are mindful of our impact and committed to being a good neighbour.

We have partnered with leading organisations on community water projects that bring clean water to people who need it most. These projects are a source of enormous pride for everyone at NorthStar, and they reflect our deep belief that access to clean water is a fundamental human right. We look forward to expanding our positive impact in the years to come.

### Packaging and the Circular Economy

We know that packaging is one of the areas where consumers most want to see change, and we are listening. NorthStar is committed to a world without waste, where every package has a second life.

We have made our bottles more sustainable through thoughtful design, using less material where we can and incorporating recycled content into our packaging. We are proud that our flagship bottle is now lighter than ever, reducing the resources needed to produce and transport it. We are also exploring exciting new materials and formats that could transform the way our products are packaged.

We firmly believe in the power of recycling, and we are working with partners across the industry to improve recycling rates and infrastructure. Our vision is a true circular economy, where the materials we use are kept in use for as long as possible. It is an ambitious vision, but we have never been afraid of ambition.

### Sustainable Sourcing

The journey to sustainability begins at the source. We are committed to sourcing our ingredients responsibly, with respect for the farmers who grow them and the land that sustains them.

We work closely with our agricultural partners to promote practices that are good for people and good for the planet. From the sugar in our drinks to the fruit in our juices, we want every ingredient to tell a story we can be proud of. We are increasing the share of our key ingredients that are sourced in line with our responsible sourcing principles, and we are encouraged by the progress our suppliers are making.

We believe that strong, long-term relationships with our suppliers are the key to a resilient and sustainable supply chain. By investing in our partners, we are investing in the future of our business and the communities that depend on it.

We are also proud to champion regenerative agriculture, an approach that holds enormous promise for soil health, biodiversity, and farmer livelihoods. We have begun working with a number of forward-thinking growers to explore how regenerative practices can be woven into our supply chain, and the early signs are genuinely inspiring. We believe this is the future of farming, and we intend to be at the forefront of it.

### Biodiversity and Nature

Nature is the foundation of everything we make. Without healthy ecosystems there would be no clean water, no fertile soil, and no thriving communities to enjoy our products. That is why protecting and restoring nature is so close to our hearts.

We are committed to being a positive force for biodiversity wherever we operate. We support a range of initiatives that protect habitats, restore landscapes, and safeguard the rich web of life that sustains us all. From planting trees to protecting watersheds, we are doing our part to help nature flourish for generations to come.

We recognise that the challenges facing the natural world are immense, and no single company can solve them alone. That is why we are proud to collaborate with conservation partners, civil society, and local communities to amplify our impact. Together, we can turn the tide for nature, and we are determined to be part of the solution.

### Innovation for Good

Innovation has always been in our DNA. We believe that the same spirit of creativity that gives the world products it loves can also help solve some of the planet's most pressing challenges. That is why we are investing in the ideas, technologies, and partnerships that will shape a more sustainable future.

Across our business, our teams are reimagining what is possible, from cleaner production methods to smarter ways of working. We are exploring exciting frontiers in materials science, renewable energy, and digital tools that help us understand and reduce our impact. We are energised by the possibilities, and we are committed to turning bold ideas into real-world progress.

We also know that the best ideas often come from unexpected places. That is why we engage with start-ups, universities, and innovators around the world, seeking out fresh thinking and new perspectives. By opening our doors to collaboration, we are accelerating the pace of change and building a more sustainable business for tomorrow.

### Engaging our Consumers

Sustainability is a shared journey, and our consumers are essential partners on the road ahead. Every day, millions of people choose NorthStar, and with that trust comes a responsibility to help them make choices that are good for them and good for the planet.

We are committed to giving our consumers the information and inspiration they need to play their part. Through our packaging, our marketing, and our digital channels, we are raising awareness of the issues that matter and encouraging more sustainable behaviours. We believe that small actions, multiplied by millions, can add up to extraordinary change.

We are also listening more closely than ever to what our consumers tell us. Their feedback shapes our priorities and pushes us to do better. We are humbled by their passion for the planet, and we are determined to be worthy of their trust.

### A Healthier Portfolio

We believe that great taste and wellbeing can go hand in hand. As tastes evolve and people seek to live healthier lives, we are proud to be evolving alongside them, offering a portfolio that gives people more of what they want and helps them feel good about their choices.

We have continued to broaden our range of options, introducing new flavours and formats designed with wellbeing in mind. We are giving consumers more choice than ever, including options with less sugar, and we are committed to clear, helpful labelling that empowers people to choose what is right for them. We want every consumer to feel that NorthStar has something for them, whatever the occasion.

Reformulating much-loved products is never easy, and we approach it with care and respect for the recipes people cherish. But we are determined to keep innovating, because we believe that doing right by our consumers and doing right by the world are one and the same. The journey towards a healthier portfolio is ongoing, and we are excited about where it will take us.

### Partnerships and Collaboration

We have always believed that the biggest challenges call for the broadest coalitions. None of us can build a sustainable future alone, and we are proud to stand shoulder to shoulder with partners who share our ambition and our values.

This year we deepened our collaboration with industry groups, non-governmental organisations, and public bodies working on the issues that matter most. By pooling our knowledge, our resources, and our reach, we are able to achieve far more together than any of us could achieve apart. These partnerships are at the very heart of how we drive change, and we are grateful for the trust and shared purpose that make them possible.

We are also committed to playing our part in the wider conversation about sustainability. We engage constructively with policymakers and stakeholders, sharing our perspective and learning from others, because we believe that progress comes from dialogue, openness, and a willingness to work together towards common goals.

### Transparency and Reporting

We know that trust must be earned, and that words must be matched by action. We are committed to being open about our journey, sharing both our achievements and the areas where we have more to do. Sustainability is not about perfection; it is about honest effort and continuous improvement, and that is the spirit in which we report our progress.

We will continue to refine how we measure and communicate our impact, drawing on emerging best practice and the expectations of our stakeholders. We want our reporting to be clear, meaningful, and genuinely useful to the many people who care about our journey. As our approach matures, so too will the way we tell our story.

Above all, we want our stakeholders to know that we take our responsibilities seriously, and that we are committed to being held to account. We welcome scrutiny, and we see it as a vital part of getting better, year after year.

### Our People and Communities

People are at the centre of everything we do. We are building a culture where every colleague feels valued, respected, and inspired to do their best work. Diversity and inclusion are not just the right thing to do; they make us stronger, more creative, and more connected to the consumers we serve.

This year we continued our investment in training and development, helping our people grow their skills and advance their careers. We are committed to health, safety, and wellbeing across our operations, because nothing matters more than the people who make NorthStar what it is.

In our communities, we are proud to support a wide range of causes through volunteering, partnerships, and charitable giving. Our colleagues gave generously of their time and talent this year, rolling up their sleeves to make a difference where it matters most. From youth education to disaster relief, we show up for the communities that have given us so much.

### Governance and Ethics

Trust is the foundation of our business. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and accountability in everything we do. Our governance framework ensures that sustainability is embedded at every level of the organisation, from the boardroom to the factory floor.

We are committed to doing business the right way, always. Our code of conduct guides our people to make ethical decisions every day, and we have robust processes in place to uphold our values. We engage openly with our stakeholders and welcome their input as we continue on our sustainability journey.

### Awards and Recognition

We are honoured that our efforts have been recognised by a number of organisations this year. These accolades are a testament to the hard work and dedication of our teams, and they inspire us to reach even higher. While awards are never the goal, they are a welcome affirmation that we are on the right track.

### Looking Ahead

We are proud of how far we have come, but we know our journey is far from over. The road ahead will not always be easy, and we will face challenges along the way. But we are more committed than ever to our vision of a brighter, more sustainable tomorrow.

In the year to come, we will deepen our commitments, strengthen our partnerships, and accelerate our progress. We will continue to listen, to learn, and to lead. And we will do it all with the optimism, passion, and purpose that define who we are.

Sustainability is the journey of a lifetime, and we are just getting started. Together, we can build a brighter tomorrow, one refreshing moment at a time. Thank you for being part of our story.

### About this Report

This report covers our global operations for the financial year. It reflects our ongoing commitment to transparency and to keeping our stakeholders informed about our sustainability journey. We welcome your feedback and look forward to sharing our continued progress in future reports.

idea:
Calls to ban generative artificial intelligence from universities have grown louder since tools that draft essays and solve problems became freely available. The impulse is understandable. Academics worry that students will outsource their thinking, that grades will stop reflecting learning, and that the value of a degree will erode. Yet a blanket ban is the wrong response. It is unenforceable, it widens existing inequalities, and it ducks the real task, which is to redesign how we assess learning. Universities should permit generative AI under clear rules and rebuild assessment around what these tools cannot do well.

Consider enforcement first. A ban only works if violations can be detected, and detection is failing. Commercial classifiers that claim to spot AI-written text produce both false positives and false negatives at rates too high for academic penalties. Some have flagged work by non-native English speakers more often, raising a fairness problem of their own. A rule that cannot be applied consistently is not a rule; it is a lottery. Worse, an unenforceable ban punishes the honest. Students who comply forgo a tool their less scrupulous peers use undetected, so the policy rewards exactly the behaviour it means to stop.

Equity deepens the objection. Banning AI on university devices and networks does not remove it from students' lives; it removes it from the supervised, documented setting where staff could teach good practice. Wealthier students will still reach premium models at home. Students juggling jobs and caring duties, who could use AI to draft an outline at midnight, lose a genuine support. A ban therefore tends to hand an advantage to those already advantaged, the opposite of what most universities claim to want.

The strongest case for permitting AI, though, is educational. The skills graduates now need include framing a problem for a model, judging whether its output is correct, and revising it. These are not trivial. Evaluating a confident but wrong answer demands exactly the disciplinary knowledge a degree is supposed to build. A course that forbids AI prepares students for a workplace that no longer exists. One that teaches critical, supervised use builds judgement that transfers.

This educational point matters most in disciplines where the hard part has never been producing text but deciding whether the text is right. A law student must learn to spot the case a model has misread; a medical student must recognise when a plausible summary omits a contraindication; an engineering student must catch a calculation that is fluent and wrong. None of that judgement is built by pretending the tool does not exist. It is built by putting students in front of imperfect machine output and asking them to find the flaw, which is exactly the kind of exercise a thoughtful curriculum can set. A ban forecloses that teaching; supervised use enables it.

None of this means assessment can stay as it is. Here the critics are right: the unsupervised take-home essay, marked as a proxy for understanding, is now a weak instrument. The answer is to change the instrument, not to police the tool. Several redesigns work. Oral examinations, in which a student defends their reasoning, are hard to fake and reveal depth quickly. In-class writing under supervision tests composition directly. Project work assessed across drafts, with a short reflective account of how AI was used, rewards process rather than a single polished artefact. Assignments can be built around materials the model has not seen, such as data the student gathered, a local case, or last week's seminar discussion. Each shifts the target from a product a machine can generate to thinking a student must demonstrate.

A fair argument deserves its counterarguments. Three are serious. First, redesign costs money and time. Oral exams do not scale cheaply to a cohort of six hundred, and overstretched departments may lack the staff. This is real, and it means the transition must be funded and phased rather than demanded overnight. Second, allowing AI may let weak students coast while appearing competent, blurring the signal a degree sends to employers. That risk is genuine, which is precisely why supervised, AI-resistant components must anchor the grade. Third, some disciplines rest on foundational skills, such as mental arithmetic or basic proof, that must be built before a tool can safely assist. For those, restricting AI in early courses is defensible. The point is that these are arguments for selective, justified limits, not for a universal ban.

There is also a softer worry that constant access to fluent text will dull students' own voices. It might. But the same was said of calculators, spell-checkers, and the web, and the sensible response each time was to teach when the tool helps and when it gets in the way, while still requiring unaided performance where it matters. That is a curriculum question, answerable course by course, not a reason to wall off the technology entirely.

What, concretely, should a university do? It should set a clear default that AI use is permitted but must be disclosed, with disclosure norms that vary by assignment. It should fund a programme to redesign high-stakes assessment towards supervised and authentic tasks over two to three years. It should train staff to use AI as a teaching aid, for instance generating practice questions or worked counter-examples. And it should keep a small set of explicitly AI-free assessments where a skill must be demonstrated unaided, named as such so the rule is transparent.

A ban offers the comfort of a clear line and the appearance of resolve. But it cannot be enforced, it falls hardest on the students with the least, and it leaves the underlying weakness in assessment untouched. The harder path, redesigning how we measure learning, is also the honest one. It treats students as people we are preparing for the world as it is, and it puts the burden of adaptation where it belongs, on the institution rather than on a rule no one can keep.

Project title: Revolutionising Healthcare Through Blockchain-Powered Patient Records

Executive summary. Healthcare is broken, and blockchain will fix it. Patient records today are trapped in silos, controlled by hospitals, and vulnerable to breaches. By moving all patient records onto a decentralised, immutable, trustless blockchain, this project will return data ownership to patients, eliminate breaches forever, and transform the entire global healthcare industry. We propose a disruptive, next-generation platform that leverages cutting-edge distributed ledger technology to create a single source of truth for every patient on the planet.

Background and motivation. The problems with current healthcare records are well known. Systems do not talk to each other. Patients cannot easily access their own data. Hackers steal millions of records every year. These problems have resisted every previous attempt at a solution, which proves that a fundamentally new paradigm is required. Blockchain is that paradigm. As the technology behind cryptocurrency, blockchain has already revolutionised finance, and healthcare is the obvious next frontier. Because the blockchain is immutable and decentralised, it removes the need for trusted intermediaries and makes data tampering impossible. This will single-handedly solve the interoperability crisis.

Proposed solution. We will build HealthChain, a blockchain platform on which every patient record is stored as an encrypted block. Each patient will hold a private key that gives them complete control over who can see their data. Smart contracts will automate consent, so that a patient can grant a doctor access with a single tap, and revoke it just as easily. Because the ledger is distributed across thousands of nodes, there is no central server to attack, and no single point of failure. The system will be fully interoperable, fully secure, and fully owned by patients. We anticipate that HealthChain will become the global standard within five years.

Technical approach. The platform will use a state-of-the-art blockchain with smart contract capability. Records will be encrypted and written to the chain. We will develop a user-friendly mobile app for patients and a dashboard for clinicians. AI and machine learning will be integrated to provide predictive analytics on the data, unlocking insights that are currently impossible. The architecture will be cloud-native, scalable, and secure by design. Further technical details will be determined during the project.

Data flows. When a patient visits a clinic, the clinician will request access through the app, the patient will approve it with their key, and the relevant blocks will be made readable to the clinician. When the visit ends, access can be revoked. Every access event will be permanently recorded on the chain, creating an unalterable audit trail. Because the record is the single source of truth, there will be no more duplicate or conflicting records across providers. Insurers, researchers, and public health agencies will be able to query anonymised data directly from the chain, unlocking value that is currently locked away in incompatible systems. The platform will support every type of medical data, from prescriptions to imaging to genomics, all on the same unified ledger.

Standards and compliance. The platform will be fully compliant with all relevant data protection regulations. Because patients control their own keys, consent is built in by design, which satisfies the spirit of every privacy law. Interoperability standards will be supported as needed. Security audits will be carried out at the appropriate time. We are confident that regulators will welcome a system that finally puts patients first, and we expect compliance to be straightforward given the inherent transparency of the blockchain.

Innovation and impact. HealthChain is the first platform to combine blockchain, AI, and healthcare in a single seamless ecosystem. The impact will be enormous. Patients will own their data. Breaches will end. Hospitals will save billions. Research will accelerate because anonymised data can flow freely. Developing countries will leapfrog legacy systems entirely. In short, this project will democratise healthcare and improve outcomes for everyone on Earth.

Team and resources. The team has strong enthusiasm for blockchain and a deep belief in its transformative potential. We will hire the necessary engineers as the project progresses. We request a budget of four million euros over three years to build the platform and bring it to market. The exact allocation of the budget will be worked out once the team is assembled, but we are confident the funding is sufficient to deliver a world-changing result.

Timeline. Year one: build the core blockchain and app. Year two: pilot with partner hospitals to be confirmed. Year three: scale globally and establish HealthChain as the world standard for patient records.

Evaluation. Success will be measured by the transformative impact of the platform and the number of patients it empowers. We are confident that the results will speak for themselves.

Risks and mitigation. We do not foresee significant risks. Blockchain is a proven technology, and our approach uses only established components. The main risk is that institutions are slow to adopt, but we will overcome this through partnerships and outreach. Privacy is fully protected by encryption and patient-held keys, so there is no meaningful risk of data exposure. Scalability is assured by the distributed nature of the platform. Should any unforeseen issues arise, the team will address them as they come up. We are confident that no obstacle is insurmountable given sufficient determination and the inherent strengths of the technology.

Sustainability. After the grant period, the platform will sustain itself through licensing fees from hospitals and value-added analytics services. Because HealthChain will be the global standard, revenue is effectively guaranteed. We may also explore a token model to incentivise participation, which would create a self-reinforcing ecosystem of patients, providers, and researchers all contributing to and benefiting from the network. The economics, like the technology, are designed to be future-proof.

Conclusion. The status quo in healthcare records is indefensible. Blockchain offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to fix it for good. With this funding, we will build the platform that finally puts patients in control and ends data breaches forever. The future of healthcare is decentralised, and that future starts here.

Executive summary. Healthcare is broken, and blockchain will fix it. Patient records today are trapped in silos, controlled by hospitals, and vulnerable to breaches. By moving all patient records onto a decentralised, immutable, trustless blockchain, this project will return data ownership to patients, eliminate breaches forever, and transform the entire global healthcare industry. We propose a disruptive, next-generation platform that leverages cutting-edge distributed ledger technology to create a single source of truth for every patient on the planet.

Background and motivation. The problems with current healthcare records are well known. Systems do not talk to each other. Patients cannot easily access their own data. Hackers steal millions of records every year. These problems have resisted every previous attempt at a solution, which proves that a fundamentally new paradigm is required. Blockchain is that paradigm. As the technology behind cryptocurrency, blockchain has already revolutionised finance, and healthcare is the obvious next frontier. Because the blockchain is immutable and decentralised, it removes the need for trusted intermediaries and makes data tampering impossible. This will single-handedly solve the interoperability crisis.

Proposed solution. We will build HealthChain, a blockchain platform on which every patient record is stored as an encrypted block. Each patient will hold a private key that gives them complete control over who can see their data. Smart contracts will automate consent, so that a patient can grant a doctor access with a single tap, and revoke it just as easily. Because the ledger is distributed across thousands of nodes, there is no central server to attack, and no single point of failure. The system will be fully interoperable, fully secure, and fully owned by patients. We anticipate that HealthChain will become the global standard within five years.

Technical approach. The platform will use a state-of-the-art blockchain with smart contract capability. Records will be encrypted and written to the chain. We will develop a user-friendly mobile app for patients and a dashboard for clinicians. AI and machine learning will be integrated to provide predictive analytics on the data, unlocking insights that are currently impossible. The architecture will be cloud-native, scalable, and secure by design. Further technical details will be determined during the project.

Data flows. When a patient visits a clinic, the clinician will request access through the app, the patient will approve it with their key, and the relevant blocks will be made readable to the clinician. When the visit ends, access can be revoked. Every access event will be permanently recorded on the chain, creating an unalterable audit trail. Because the record is the single source of truth, there will be no more duplicate or conflicting records across providers. Insurers, researchers, and public health agencies will be able to query anonymised data directly from the chain, unlocking value that is currently locked away in incompatible systems. The platform will support every type of medical data, from prescriptions to imaging to genomics, all on the same unified ledger.

Standards and compliance. The platform will be fully compliant with all relevant data protection regulations. Because patients control their own keys, consent is built in by design, which satisfies the spirit of every privacy law. Interoperability standards will be supported as needed. Security audits will be carried out at the appropriate time. We are confident that regulators will welcome a system that finally puts patients first, and we expect compliance to be straightforward given the inherent transparency of the blockchain.

Innovation and impact. HealthChain is the first platform to combine blockchain, AI, and healthcare in a single seamless ecosystem. The impact will be enormous. Patients will own their data. Breaches will end. Hospitals will save billions. Research will accelerate because anonymised data can flow freely. Developing countries will leapfrog legacy systems entirely. In short, this project will democratise healthcare and improve outcomes for everyone on Earth.

Team and resources. The team has strong enthusiasm for blockchain and a deep belief in its transformative potential. We will hire the necessary engineers as the project progresses. We request a budget of four million euros over three years to build the platform and bring it to market. The exact allocation of the budget will be worked out once the team is assembled, but we are confident the funding is sufficient to deliver a world-changing result.

Timeline. Year one: build the core blockchain and app. Year two: pilot with partner hospitals to be confirmed. Year three: scale globally and establish HealthChain as the world standard for patient records.

Evaluation. Success will be measured by the transformative impact of the platform and the number of patients it empowers. We are confident that the results will speak for themselves.

Risks and mitigation. We do not foresee significant risks. Blockchain is a proven technology, and our approach uses only established components. The main risk is that institutions are slow to adopt, but we will overcome this through partnerships and outreach. Privacy is fully protected by encryption and patient-held keys, so there is no meaningful risk of data exposure. Scalability is assured by the distributed nature of the platform. Should any unforeseen issues arise, the team will address them as they come up. We are confident that no obstacle is insurmountable given sufficient determination and the inherent strengths of the technology.

Sustainability. After the grant period, the platform will sustain itself through licensing fees from hospitals and value-added analytics services. Because HealthChain will be the global standard, revenue is effectively guaranteed. We may also explore a token model to incentivise participation, which would create a self-reinforcing ecosystem of patients, providers, and researchers all contributing to and benefiting from the network. The economics, like the technology, are designed to be future-proof.

Conclusion. The status quo in healthcare records is indefensible. Blockchain offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to fix it for good. With this funding, we will build the platform that finally puts patients in control and ends data breaches forever. The future of healthcare is decentralised, and that future starts here.

By moving all patient records onto a decentralised, immutable, trustless blockchain, this project will return data ownership to patients, eliminate breaches forever, and transform the entire global healthcare industry. We propose a disruptive, next-generation platform that leverages cutting-edge distributed ledger technology to create a single source of truth for every patient on the planet.

Background and motivation. The problems with current healthcare records are well known. Systems do not talk to each other. Patients cannot easily access their own data. Hackers steal millions of records every year. These problems have resisted every previous attempt at a solution, which proves that a fundamentally new paradigm is required. Blockchain is that paradigm. As the technology behind cryptocurrency, blockchain has already revolutionised finance, and healthcare is the obvious next frontier. Because the blockchain is immutable and decentralised, it removes the need for trusted intermediaries and makes data tampering impossible. This will single-handedly solve the interoperability crisis.

Proposed solution. We will build HealthChain, a blockchain platform on which every patient record is stored as an encrypted block. Each patient will hold a private key that gives them complete control over who can see their data. Smart contracts will automate consent, so that a patient can grant a doctor access with a single tap, and revoke it just as easily. Because the ledger is distributed across thousands of nodes, there is no central server to attack, and no single point of failure. The system will be fully interoperable, fully secure, and fully owned by patients. We anticipate that HealthChain will become the global standard within five years.

Technical approach. The platform will use a state-of-the-art blockchain with smart contract capability. Records will be encrypted and written to the chain. We will develop a user-friendly mobile app for patients and a dashboard for clinicians. AI and machine learning will be integrated to provide predictive analytics on the data, unlocking insights that are currently impossible. The architecture will be cloud-native, scalable, and secure by design. Further technical details will be determined during the project.

Data flows. When a patient visits a clinic, the clinician will request access through the app, the patient will approve it with their key, and the relevant blocks will be made readable to the clinician. When the visit ends, access can be revoked. Every access event will be permanently recorded on the chain, creating an unalterable audit trail. Because the record is the single source of truth, there will be no more duplicate or conflicting records across providers. Insurers, researchers, and public health agencies will be able to query anonymised data directly from the chain, unlocking value that is currently locked away in incompatible systems. The platform will support every type of medical data, from prescriptions to imaging to genomics, all on the same unified ledger.

Standards and compliance. The platform will be fully compliant with all relevant data protection regulations. Because patients control their own keys, consent is built in by design, which satisfies the spirit of every privacy law. Interoperability standards will be supported as needed. Security audits will be carried out at the appropriate time. We are confident that regulators will welcome a system that finally puts patients first, and we expect compliance to be straightforward given the inherent transparency of the blockchain.

Innovation and impact. HealthChain is the first platform to combine blockchain, AI, and healthcare in a single seamless ecosystem. The impact will be enormous. Patients will own their data. Breaches will end. Hospitals will save billions. Research will accelerate because anonymised data can flow freely. Developing countries will leapfrog legacy systems entirely. In short, this project will democratise healthcare and improve outcomes for everyone on Earth.

Team and resources. The team has strong enthusiasm for blockchain and a deep belief in its transformative potential. We will hire the necessary engineers as the project progresses. We request a budget of four million euros over three years to build the platform and bring it to market. The exact allocation of the budget will be worked out once the team is assembled, but we are confident the funding is sufficient to deliver a world-changing result.

Timeline. Year one: build the core blockchain and app. Year two: pilot with partner hospitals to be confirmed. Year three: scale globally and establish HealthChain as the world standard for patient records.

Evaluation. Success will be measured by the transformative impact of the platform and the number of patients it empowers. We are confident that the results will speak for themselves.

Risks and mitigation. We do not foresee significant risks. Blockchain is a proven technology, and our approach uses only established components. The main risk is that institutions are slow to adopt, but we will overcome this through partnerships and outreach. Privacy is fully protected by encryption and patient-held keys, so there is no meaningful risk of data exposure. Scalability is assured by the distributed nature of the platform. Should any unforeseen issues arise, the team will address them as they come up. We are confident that no obstacle is insurmountable given sufficient determination and the inherent strengths of the technology.

Sustainability. After the grant period, the platform will sustain itself through licensing fees from hospitals and value-added analytics services. Because HealthChain will be the global standard, revenue is effectively guaranteed. We may also explore a token model to incentivise participation, which would create a self-reinforcing ecosystem of patients, providers, and researchers all contributing to and benefiting from the network. The economics, like the technology, are designed to be future-proof.

Conclusion. The status quo in healthcare records is indefensible. Blockchain offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to fix it for good. With this funding, we will build the platform that finally puts patients in control and ends data breaches forever. The future of healthcare is decentralised, and that future starts here.

Executive summary. Healthcare is broken, and blockchain will fix it. Patient records today are trapped in silos, controlled by hospitals, and vulnerable to breaches. By moving all patient records onto a decentralised, immutable, trustless blockchain, this project will return data ownership to patients, eliminate breaches forever, and transform the entire global healthcare industry. We propose a disruptive, next-generation platform that leverages cutting-edge distributed ledger technology to create a single source of truth for every patient on the planet.

Background and motivation. The problems with current healthcare records are well known. Systems do not talk to each other. Patients cannot easily access their own data. Hackers steal millions of records every year. These problems have resisted every previous attempt at a solution, which proves that a fundamentally new paradigm is required. Blockchain is that paradigm. As the technology behind cryptocurrency, blockchain has already revolutionised finance, and healthcare is the obvious next frontier. Because the blockchain is immutable and decentralised, it removes the need for trusted intermediaries and makes data tampering impossible. This will single-handedly solve the interoperability crisis.

Proposed solution. We will build HealthChain, a blockchain platform on which every patient record is stored as an encrypted block. Each patient will hold a private key that gives them complete control over who can see their data. Smart contracts will automate consent, so that a patient can grant a doctor access with a single tap, and revoke it just as easily. Because the ledger is distributed across thousands of nodes, there is no central server to attack, and no single point of failure. The system will be fully interoperable, fully secure, and fully owned by patients. We anticipate that HealthChain will become the global standard within five years.

Technical approach. The platform will use a state-of-the-art blockchain with smart contract capability. Records will be encrypted and written to the chain. We will develop a user-friendly mobile app for patients and a dashboard for clinicians. AI and machine learning will be integrated to provide predictive analytics on the data, unlocking insights that are currently impossible. The architecture will be cloud-native, scalable, and secure by design. Further technical details will be determined during the project.

Data flows. When a patient visits a clinic, the clinician will request access through the app, the patient will approve it with their key, and the relevant blocks will be made readable to the clinician. When the visit ends, access can be revoked. Every access event will be permanently recorded on the chain, creating an unalterable audit trail. Because the record is the single source of truth, there will be no more duplicate or conflicting records across providers. Insurers, researchers, and public health agencies will be able to query anonymised data directly from the chain, unlocking value that is currently locked away in incompatible systems. The platform will support every type of medical data, from prescriptions to imaging to genomics, all on the same unified ledger.

Standards and compliance. The platform will be fully compliant with all relevant data protection regulations. Because patients control their own keys, consent is built in by design, which satisfies the spirit of every privacy law. Interoperability standards will be supported as needed. Security audits will be carried out at the appropriate time. We are confident that regulators will welcome a system that finally puts patients first, and we expect compliance to be straightforward given the inherent transparency of the blockchain.

Innovation and impact. HealthChain is the first platform to combine blockchain, AI, and healthcare in a single seamless ecosystem. The impact will be enormous. Patients will own their data. Breaches will end. Hospitals will save billions. Research will accelerate because anonymised data can flow freely. Developing countries will leapfrog legacy systems entirely. In short, this project will democratise healthcare and improve outcomes for everyone on Earth.

Team and resources. The team has strong enthusiasm for blockchain and a deep belief in its transformative potential. We will hire the necessary engineers as the project progresses. We request a budget of four million euros over three years to build the platform and bring it to market. The exact allocation of the budget will be worked out once the team is assembled, but we are confident the funding is sufficient to deliver a world-changing result.

Timeline. Year one: build the core blockchain and app. Year two: pilot with partner hospitals to be confirmed. Year three: scale globally and establish HealthChain as the world standard for patient records.

Evaluation. Success will be measured by the transformative impact of the platform and the number of patients it empowers. We are confident that the results will speak for themselves.

Risks and mitigation. We do not foresee significant risks. Blockchain is a proven technology, and our approach uses only established components. The main risk is that institutions are slow to adopt, but we will overcome this through partnerships and outreach. Privacy is fully protected by encryption and patient-held keys, so there is no meaningful risk of data exposure. Scalability is assured by the distributed nature of the platform. Should any unforeseen issues arise, the team will address them as they come up. We are confident that no obstacle is insurmountable given sufficient determination and the inherent strengths of the technology.

Sustainability. After the grant period, the platform will sustain itself through licensing fees from hospitals and value-added analytics services. Because HealthChain will be the global standard, revenue is effectively guaranteed. We may also explore a token model to incentivise participation, which would create a self-reinforcing ecosystem of patients, providers, and researchers all contributing to and benefiting from the network. The economics, like the technology, are designed to be future-proof.

Conclusion. The status quo in healthcare records is indefensible. Blockchain offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to fix it for good. With this funding, we will build the platform that finally puts patients in control and ends data breaches forever. The future of healthcare is decentralised, and that future starts here.
